_comment: user_agent: a browser User-Agent for every link checked. Sites increasingly
answer an unrecognised agent with 403, and a 403 that only a bot ever sees
is not a dead link. Setting the agent is the accurate fix; widening
aliveStatusCodes to accept 403 would suppress genuine breakage instead.
It must be the top-level `user_agent` key, NOT an httpHeaders entry.
link-check hands needle a `user_agent` option that defaults to
'link-check/<version>', and needle applies that over anything set through
headers -- so a User-Agent placed in httpHeaders is silently discarded.
This was verified both ways.
ivarjacobson.com is ignored because it is intermittent, not because it is
dead: the same URL was observed returning 200, then 403, then 200 from the
same workstation minutes apart, and separately 403 on a CI runner. The page
is alive -- checked by hand. link-check retries only a 429, so retryCount
cannot absorb a 403, and an intermittent failure in a pre-commit hook
blocks a commit that has nothing to do with it. A check that fails at
random teaches people to bypass it, which costs more than the one link it
was watching. Scoped to this host, so a 403 anywhere else still fails.
martinfowler.com is ignored because this network cannot reach it, not
because it is dead: the three cited pages were opened by hand in a browser
and load normally. What was observed from the workstation on 2026-08-31 is
a connection-level failure -- DNS resolves to 34.198.71.201, and a TCP
connect to :443 times out after 15s even when pointed straight at that
address, with and without a browser User-Agent. It is host-specific rather
than an egress problem: example.com, github.com, google.com, pypi.org and
cdn.jsdelivr.net all answered in under five seconds from the same shell,
minutes apart. A silent timeout is what a drop rule looks like; whether the
block is at the site's front or somewhere on this path is not knowable from
here.
retryCount cannot absorb it -- link-check retries only a 429 -- and the
hook runs on every commit that touches a file citing these links, so a
reference added in 2026 blocks unrelated work indefinitely. Scoped to this
host, so a dead link anywhere else still fails.
REVISIT: unlike the ivarjacobson entry, this one was NOT observed failing
on a CI runner -- only from one workstation. GitHub's runners have wider
egress and may well reach the site, in which case this entry is suppressing
a check that would otherwise work in the scheduled links.yml job. Drop it
and watch one scheduled run before assuming it is needed there too.
TEMPORARY: the scorecard entry. A workflow's badge.svg 404s until that
workflow has run at least once, and scorecard.yaml runs only on a push to
the default branch, so it cannot have run from a feature branch. Delete
that entry after the first scorecard run on the default branch. The blanket
ignore that covered this repository's own GitHub URLs while it had no
remote is gone -- those resolve now and are checked again.
